asks: A labelled diagram of three equal paper strips one below the other, cut into halves, quarters and eighths, with one half, two quarters and four eighths shaded.
A drawing of a round roti cut into two equal halves, and beside it an equal roti cut into four equal quarters, with one half and two quarters shaded.
picture.why: Equal strips lined up show at a glance that one half, two quarters and four eighths cover the same length.

big_idea.text: Different fractions such as 1/2, 2/4 and 4/8 can name exactly the same amount.

objectives.can: Make an equivalent fraction by multiplying the top and bottom by the same number
Explain why 2/4 is the same amount as 1/2
Compare fractions with bigger numbers by the amount they show

why_it_matters.text: It lets you see that half a packet and two quarters of a packet are the same, and it is the step that lets you add and compare fractions.

the_why.text: Cutting every piece of a strip into two equal smaller pieces doubles the number of pieces in the whole and doubles the number shaded, but the shaded length does not change, so 1/2 and 2/4 are the same amount.

picture.text: One strip with half shaded. A line cuts each half into two: now 2 of 4 parts are shaded, and the shaded length has not moved. Another cut makes 4 of 8. The three strips line up one below another; the shaded parts end at the same place.

card.diagram_ask: A labelled diagram of three equal paper strips one below the other, cut into halves, quarters and eighths, with one half, two quarters and four eighths shaded.

needs_first.text: What the top and bottom numbers of a fraction mean.
Halves and quarters of a shape are equal parts.

mistakes.mistake: Thinking 4/8 is more than 1/2 because 4 and 8 are bigger numbers.
mistakes.why_it_fails: The bigger numbers count smaller pieces: 8 small pieces make the whole, so 4 of them are still half.

mistakes.mistake: Adding the same number to top and bottom: 1/2 = 2/3.
mistakes.why_it_fails: 2/3 covers more of the strip than 1/2; only multiplying both by the same number cuts every piece the same way.
Cutting the pieces smaller without counting the new shaded pieces makes the shaded part half as big.

opening_question.question: Asha eats 1/2 of a chikki bar and Ravi eats 2/4 of the same size bar. Who ate more?
guesses: Asha, because halves are big pieces
opening_question.answer: Both ate the same amount: 2/4 is the same as 1/2.

route.what: Show a strip with half shaded and ask whether 2/4 of the same strip is more, less or the same. Ask for a guess.
Cut each half of the strip into two: now 4 parts, 2 shaded. The shaded length did not move.
Ask: when each piece is cut in two, what happens to the shaded pieces and the whole? Both counts double, but the amount stays.
Cut again: 4 of 8 parts shaded. Line the three strips up: the shaded parts end at the same place.
Name them equivalent fractions, and write the rule: multiply top and bottom by the same number.
Try 1/2 = 2/3 by adding 1 to each: the 2/3 strip's shading goes further. Adding does not work; multiplying does.
Find a fraction equal to 3/4 with 8 at the bottom (6/8) before it is shown.
The learner says why 2/4 is the same as 1/2.

questions.question: Which fraction is the same amount as 2/3?
questions.explain: Cutting each third into two gives 4 of 6 pieces; 3/4 adds one to each, and 2/6 changes only the bottom.

questions.question: Is 4/8 more than, less than, or the same as 1/2?
options: More, because 4 and 8 are bigger numbers
Less, because eighths are small pieces
questions.explain: Four eighths cover exactly half the strip: more pieces, but each piece is smaller.

try_it.title: Fold the strips
try_it.stands_for: Each strip is one whole; each fold cuts every piece into two equal smaller pieces.
try_it.predict: Will the shaded part of 4/8 end before, at, or after the shaded part of 1/2?
steps: Fold the first strip in half once, open it and shade one part.
Fold the second strip in half twice, open it and shade two parts.
Fold the third strip in half three times, open it and shade four parts.
Lay the three strips one below another, lined up at the left edge.
try_it.observe: The shaded parts of all three strips end at the same place, exactly in the middle.
try_it.question: Why do one half, two quarters and four eighths cover the same length?
try_it.expected: Because each fold cuts every piece into two, so the number of pieces in the whole and the number shaded both double, while the shaded length stays the same.
try_it.write: 1/2, 2/4 and 4/8 are the same amount. Multiplying the top and bottom by the same number gives an equivalent fraction.
try_it.in_class: Pairs, three strips each. The teacher draws a fraction wall of halves, quarters and eighths on the board. Ask: which is more, 1/2 or 4/8, and why? A class that says 4/8 is reading the numbers, not the strip.
